title: RBAC v2 event contracts and evidence handoff spec
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines the canonical event contracts for RBAC v2 telemetry, describes the handoff artifacts required by our evidence automation pipeline, and prescribes a staged rollout plan that minimizes forensics gaps during migration. It is intended for engineering owners (auth, api-gateway), SRE, compliance, and the SIEM integration team.

Background and motivation:
- RBAC v2 introduces attribute-centric bindings, delegation tokens, and ephemeral grants for dedicated and private deployments. Existing audit exports capture coarse permission-change events but lack consistent context for automated evidence extracts (policy snapshots, pre-change principals, CPI counters).
- Security reviews and SOC audits require: (1) reconstructable state at time T, (2) machine-readable event payloads to support automated evidence bundling, and (3) deterministic mapping to SIEM fields.

Goals:
- Define a small, stable set of event types for RBAC lifecycle (ROLE_CREATE, ROLE_UPDATE, BINDING_CREATE, BINDING_REVOKE, DELEGATION_ISSUE, DELEGATION_REVOKE, AUTHZ_CHECK, IMPERSONATION_START/END).
- Require consistent context payloads that allow evidence automation to collect: policy snapshot, pre/post binding diffs, requester metadata, and correlated request traces.
- Provide an Elastic Common Schema (ECS) mapping for SIEM export and an ingest-friendly sample set for testing.
- Provide a safe, incremental rollout that preserves forensic coverage.

Event contract principles (high level):
- Events must be append-only canonical logs emitted by the authoritative auth service. No derived or aggregated events as source-of-truth.
- Each event must include: event_id (UUIDv4), occurred_at (ISO8601), actor (principal id + type), target (role/binding id + type), request_context (route, request_id, trace_id), policy_snapshot_ref (immutable hash or object id), and outcome (success|failure|partial).
- Minimize PII: include internal IDs; faceted display names only where needed and marked as redaction-friendly.
- Provide a short, stable schema version string in events (rbac_v2.v1).

Minimal canonical schema (example payload as plain text):
{ "event_id": "uuid-1234-abcd", "schema": "rbac_v2.v1", "event_type": "BINDING_CREATE", "occurred_at": "2024-12-11T18:22:37Z", "actor": { "id": "user:ashapatel", "type": "user", "auth_level": "2fa" }, "target": { "id": "binding:bind-87", "object": "role", "role_id": "role:dedicated-admin" }, "request_context": { "request_id": "req-90e7", "trace_id": "trace-555", "api_route": "POST /v1/admin/bindings" }, "policy_snapshot_ref": "sha256:abcd...", "diff_summary": "added principal user:svc-qa to role:dedicated-admin", "outcome": "success", "evidence_refs": ["evidence:12345"] }

Note: The actual stored event must be a single-line JSON in the audit store. The multiline example above is for human readability. The event payload must keep the same key names and value types across versions; when changes are necessary, increment the schema string.

Evidence automation handoff contract:
- For non-trivial RBAC changes (any binding create/delete, delegation issue/revoke, role schema change), the auth service must atomically produce an evidence bundle and emit a pointer in the event payload (evidence_refs).
- Evidence bundle contents (artifact IDs or object store paths):
  - policy_snapshot.json (full policy graph as of occurred_at)
  - pre_change_state.json (if change has pre-state)
  - post_change_state.json (if applicable)
  - request_trace.log (raw request logs correlated by trace_id)
  - human_readable_summary.txt (one-line summary + operator notes if any)
  - captured_kms_key_info.txt (for actions related to private deployments)
- Bundles must be stored under an immutable object store path with write-once semantics and TTL controlled by compliance (default 3 years for enterprise customers). The evidence_refs array should include stable object IDs and a short integrity hash for quick validation.

SIEM export mapping (recommended ECS mapping):
- Map event_id -> event.id, occurred_at -> @timestamp, actor.id -> user.id, actor.type -> user.type, target.role_id -> authorization.role, request_context.trace_id -> trace.id, policy_snapshot_ref -> file.hash.sha256, outcome -> event.outcome, schema -> event.dataset.
- Add a custom field: rbcd.rbac_schema_version = rbac_v2.v1 (for query filtering).
- When exporting to SIEM, include evidence_refs as an array of urls under rbcd.evidence_urls and the evidence bundle integrity hash under rbcd.evidence_hash.

Sample exported ECS event (flattened for SIEM):
{ "@timestamp": "2024-12-11T18:22:37Z", "event.id": "uuid-1234-abcd", "event.dataset": "rbac_v2.v1", "event.action": "binding.create", "user.id": "user:ashapatel", "user.type": "user", "authorization.role": "role:dedicated-admin", "trace.id": "trace-555", "rbcd.evidence_urls": ["s3://evidence-prod/2024/12/11/evidence-12345.tar.gz"], "rbcd.evidence_hash": "sha256:abcd...", "event.outcome": "success" }

Retention, sampling, and aggregation guidelines:
- Full bundle retention default: 3 years for enterprise customers; 1 year for standard hosted API.
- For high-volume ephemeral events (authz checks at token-level) we must not create full evidence bundles. Instead: export aggregated counters daily and sample full traces under a deterministic sampler (e.g., 1 in 1000 or keyed sampler based on principal hash) with configurable rate per customer class.
- All binding and delegation lifecycle changes are not sampled — they always produce bundles.

Rollout and migration plan (phased):
Phase 0 — Canary (2 weeks):
- Enable RBAC v2 event contracts behind feature flag on staging. Emit events to a staging audit topic and run the evidence bundler to the staging object store.
- Verify ECS mapping and ingestion into a staging SIEM index.
- Owners: Ravi (auth), Asha (evidence-bundler), Marta (SIEM).

Phase 1 — Pilot customers (4 weeks):
- Turn on RBAC v2 events for 3 low-risk internal tenants and one external pilot.
- Run parity checks: every historical change must be reconstructable from the new bundles.
- End-to-end verification: sample 50 lifecycle ops and run forensic reconstruction.

Phase 2 — Wide internal (4 weeks):
- Turn on for all internal orgs. Start exporting to production SIEM indices with a controlled prefix (rbac-v2-pilot-*).
- Enable automated regression alerts for missing evidence_refs or bundle store failures.

Phase 3 — Global rollout (8 weeks):
- Gradually enable for external customers by region, aligned with dedicated/private rollout windows.
- Provide customers with a migration advisory and evidence retention contract summary.

Migration checklist (operational):
- [ ] Feature flag gating implemented in auth service and gateway.
- [ ] Evidence bundler supports policy_snapshot and pre/post diffs.
- [ ] Object store lifecycle and encryption policies verified with compliance.
- [ ] SIEM parsers updated and acceptance tests added.
- [ ] Monitoring/alerts for bundler failures and event emission gaps.
- [ ] Runbooks for incident response and forensic reconstruction written and attached.

Forensic reconstruction runbook (short):
1) Given an incident and a time T, query audit-store for all RBAC v2 events with occurred_at in +/- 5 minutes of T and matching principal ids.
2) Fetch policy_snapshot_ref objects and pre/post states from object store using evidence_refs.
3) Re-run local policy evaluation against snapshot to reconstruct effective authorizations.
4) Correlate with request traces and SRE logs for request-level detail.
5) Produce a report: timeline, actors, actions, reconstructed_effective_permissions, and recommended remediation.

Testing and validation matrix (samples):
- Unit tests: schema validation, redaction, evidence_refs formatting.
- Integration tests: bundler end-to-end, SIEM ingest mapping, ECS fields present and correctly typed.
- Load tests: emit 10k events/s with high authz-check ratios to verify sampling logic and ensure bundler does not OOM.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: evidence bundler becomes a throughput bottleneck. Mitigation: async write with backpressure to audit topic and circuit-breaker policy; degrade to minimal event with reference to queued bundle work item.
- Risk: excessive storage costs from long-lived bundles. Mitigation: TTL per-customer class + compressed delta snapshots instead of complete policy dumps for frequent minor changes.
- Risk: SIEM schemas drift. Mitigation: schema version field and daily validation job that rejects unknown keys.

Open questions (to resolve before Phase 2):
- Should policy snapshots include a full flattened graph for private deployments (regulatory) even if larger? Proposal: enable full dumps for private customers by default, but compress and encrypt with customer KMS.
- How should we represent delegated grants that are time-windowed and partially overlapping? Need canonical canonicalization for pre/post diffs.
- What set of principals should be exempt from sampling (service accounts vs user accounts)?

Next actions and owners (short):
- Ravi: implement schema wiring in auth service and add schema version field (due 2024-12-20).
- Asha: extend evidence-bundler to emit immutable object paths and integrity hashes (due 2025-01-10).
- Marta: prepare SIEM ingest tests and mapping docs (due 2024-12-22).
- Elliot: prepare load test harness and sampling verification (due 2025-01-05).

Appendix: quick checklist for developers adding RBAC events:
1) Use provided schema constants from infra/schema/rbac_v2.json.
2) Emit event as single-line JSON to audit topic; include policy_snapshot_ref if action mutates state.
3) Attach trace_id and request_id for every event; link to existing tracing system.
4) Never include raw user email or external IDs — use internal stable ids and a display_name field that is redaction-friendly.

Document history: initial draft 2024-11-15 by Ravi Kapoor; collaborators Asha Patel, Marta Novak, Elliot Green.
